comment: Hand-written cases outside the trace fixtures. Every trace in tests/fixtures/harness*/ is a case 'trace/<name>' added by the generator. Kinds: official_trace (recorded on the official server and replayed by Circuit), black_box (the same client script against the official server and Circuit, outputs compared), real_client (the unmodified client against Circuit only), round_trip (data through the official server and back), planned (an acceptance case with no expectation recorded yet).

cases.description: 48 steps: every click mode in a chest, the own window, a double chest and a hopper, throws and pickups

26 steps in furnace, smoker and blast furnace windows: their window types, the fuel and result slots refusing stone, shift-clicks routed by recipe and fuel (a bucket is no fuel to shift-click), cooking in the window, taking and shift-clicking results, and the burn and cooking times the windows show
Wall correction, falls, regeneration, death, respawn, the void and the floating kick
19 moves against a chest, repeaters, a hopper and a full block
Seven chest placement and pairing cases
Player placement of dust, levers, a step, a wall lever and repeaters

Player placement of full blocks, soul sand and mud, pillars on every face, stairs facing four ways and in both halves, slabs in both halves and doubled from the clicked slab and beside it, fences, panes, bars and walls beside blocks and each other, blocks facing the player, end rods and lightning rods (an end rod on an end rod), observers looking each way, trapdoors on a side's halves, torches, lanterns, ladders, carpets, flowers and a sapling where supported and a flower where not, doors clicked in either half, beside stone and beside another door, tall flowers on dirt and where they have no soil, furnaces, barrels, shulker boxes and eleven other blocks with block entities, signs, a banner and heads turned at yaws between the four sides, a wall sign, a wall banner and a wall head, a bed and a bed whose head is blocked, and nine of them into water sources: 148 placed states identical with both official servers

Players stacking snow layers from one to eight and a ninth above them, snow on grass, ice, a bottom slab and beside a layer, stone, a torch, a lantern and planks placed at a single layer and stone onto two, snow blocks on the floor and into a layer: 40 placed states identical with both official servers
Six pass/fail checks calibrated on the official server, then run against Circuit
66 steps of walking, jumping, sprinting, falling, death and respawning
Repeater lines, pistons and a second player
A world exported by Circuit, opened and saved by the official server, imported again
TNT placement, breaking and every ignition path
Primed TNT creation order, fuse, motion, collision and removal
Primed TNT on the ground, in the air, in water and at chunk edges

The tntExplodes game rule on and off (1.21.8 only)
A named TNT duplication design (the Mytteri push duper) over repeated cycles
The duplication machine at chunk edges and corners (official traces), across region layouts and restarts (restored engines continue exactly)

Item stacks with components that the official servers sent after /give: 36 stacks with 93 of 96 component types (1.21.8) and 31 with 65 of 67 (1.21.4) are read, checked, written back in canonical form and read again (protocol_tests)
Creative slots with a custom name and a potion are kept and sent back with their components; an enchanted book is refused because the enchantment registry is not synchronized

A world saved by the official server with a named chest, items with a custom name, lore, damage, rarity and glint, and a sign with text: imported by Circuit, shown to a client with the chest title and the components, exported and read back by the official server unchanged; a second world with a trimmed chestplate and a banner with patterns and a base color likewise

Every registry Circuit synchronizes has the same entries as the official server's configuration, and the bundles' game rules are the official /gamerule lists (server_tests); registries not sent are listed

cases.location: tests/data/data_tests.cpp with the operator's jars; external: client harness smoke with vanilla-server-jar
cases.description: The official jars' built-in packs load (SHA-1 and version.json checked); each registry Circuit numbers has as many tags as the official servers send; the unmodified clients of both versions join with the enchantment registry and every tag; enchanted items round-trip through Anvil and the official server

cases.location: external: circuit-clienttest/craft-loot.js (craft); tests/fixtures/crafting/own-window.tsv, replayed by tests/server/server_tests.cpp with the operator's 1.21.8 jar
cases.description: 48 steps in the own window: results following the grid, taking them by click, right click, shift-click (also with room for part of the result), number key and throwing, mirrored shapes, honey bottle remainders, transmuting a shulker box and refusing to transmute a box into itself; Circuit and both official servers give identical windows

47 steps at crafting tables: shift-clicks into the grid and out of it, results by click, number key and shift-click (crafting until the result changes), drags over the grid, remainders, the grid given back on closing and when a creative player breaks the table, dropped when the player dies and when they leave (with the own grid's items); Circuit and both official servers give identical windows, inventories and drops

27 steps at a stonecutter: shift-clicks into the input by recipe and across the inventory, recipe buttons (one beyond the list), results by click, onto the cursor, by number key and shift-clicked until the input runs out, another item clearing the choice, the input given back on closing and dropped when the player leaves; and the update_recipes packet (254 stonecutter recipes in order, seven property sets) equal to both official servers'

24 steps at a smithing table: shift-clicks into the template, base and addition slots and across the inventory (an item whose slot holds another), a netherite upgrade keeping an enchantment, a coast trim of netherite and of iron (the trim components' registry ids), the same trim again making nothing, results by click, shift-click and number key, stone refused by every slot, the inputs given back on closing; Circuit and both official servers give identical windows

20 steps in a crafter's window: its type and slots, shift-clicks into the first enabled slot and out to the hotbar's end, an empty slot disabled and enabled again, a slot holding logs refusing to be disabled, a disabled slot refusing items, the result shown and refusing clicks, the window's ten properties (disabled slots, triggered) kept across closing; Circuit and both official servers give identical windows

25 steps at a grindstone: a cursed and enchanted pickaxe disenchanted (the curse and a repair cost of 1 kept), two damaged pickaxes merged, enchanted books into books (1.21.4 keeps an empty stored_enchantments, 1.21.8 none), a plain damaged pickaxe alone making nothing, quick moves into both inputs and across, stone refused, closing; experience orbs left out; Circuit and both official servers give identical windows

48 steps at an anvil placed across the player's way: a worn iron pickaxe repaired by three ingots, two pickaxes combined, Efficiency I and a book of it made Efficiency II, names typed and kept for the next items (a blank one removing a name, one too long ignored, a section sign removed), renaming alone capped at 39 levels with prior work penalties, a repair too expensive at 41, a result refused with too few levels and taken with enough, then /xp adding and setting levels and points (the total wrapping at the largest int); Circuit and both official servers give identical windows, costs, components, levels, progress and totals

An enchanting table with 0 to 16 bookshelves placed around it, a stone halfway to three of them and two raised ones: the ten window properties for 35 items (costs, the seed's low bits, the clues), lapis and items moved in and out, an offer refused with too few levels and too little lapis, a diamond sword enchanted by the third offer for 3 levels and 3 lapis, an enchanted item offered nothing, and enchanting in creative mode, with the player's enchantment seed set on the official servers to Circuit's; enchantments are compared as sets (the official servers send them in a hash order); Circuit and both official servers give identical output, and 320 windows recorded with two other seeds match the fitted model

22 steps at a lectern with a comparator reading it: placed facing the player, a plain book refused, a three-page writable book put on and used up, its window (type 17, the book, the page property), next and previous pages with their pulses and the comparator's 1, 8 and 15, pages by number (clamped to the book), the book taken by its button into the inventory and the window closed, a one-page book reading 15, the lectern broken dropping itself and its book, a book put on in creative mode kept in the hand, and a click on the window's book slot taking the book; Circuit and both official servers give identical output

14 steps with two players and a scene built with /setblock: a trapped chest opened by one player and then the other, an item moved in, each closing it; a double trapped chest opened and closed; a barrel and a chest opened and closed; the power of dust beside the trapped chest and beside the block below it, the dust beside the double trapped chest and a comparator reading the trapped chest, and the lid block events (positions, counts and rechecks) the first player receives; Circuit and both official servers give identical output

12 steps for a trapped chest and then a barrel: opened, the player walking 6 blocks away with the window open and back, closed, opened and closed again; the power beside the trapped chest, the barrel's open state, the window and the lid events received (the player stays a viewer while the window is open); Circuit and both official servers give identical output

5 steps at a barrel under a stone with a comparator reading it: its window (type 2, title container.barrel, 63 slots) opening the barrel, three stacks moved in by shift-clicks (the comparator 2), closed, and broken in survival dropping itself and its contents (totals by item, the stacks splitting at random); Circuit and both official servers give identical output

The window type and title of 19 containers and workstations opened once (chest, trapped chest, barrel, hopper, dispenser, dropper, furnace, smoker, blast furnace, crafter, brewing stand, crafting table, stonecutter, smithing table, grindstone, loom, anvil, enchanting table and a double chest): each title is a translation, as is a lectern's (titles-lectern.js, container.lectern); Circuit and both official servers give identical output

9 steps of a survival player at a composter with a comparator behind it: a seed into an empty composter (always a layer), dirt placed on it, pumpkin pies until level 7 (each a layer, used up), a pie at level 7 taking nothing, ready a second later, emptied by hand dropping its bone meal; the level, the held stack, the dust's power and the level events (1500 with 1 or 0) the player receives; Circuit and both official servers give identical output

9 steps with two players, two ender chests and one under a stone: the first player's window (type 2, title container.enderchest, 63 slots), two stacks shift-clicked in, the second player's window at the same ender chest (their own, empty), both closing, the first player's window at the other ender chest holding the two stacks, and no window under the stone; the lid events and counts (a recheck every 5 ticks as for chests), a comparator behind an ender chest reading nothing; Circuit and both official servers give identical output

12 steps at shulker boxes facing up and north, one with a stone over its lid and one under a hopper: a window (type 20, container.shulkerBox), iron and planks shift-clicked in and a shulker box refused, its lid events (on opening and closing only), a comparator reading it, the boxes kept shut by the stone over the lid and by the hopper but not by a stone beside the lid, the filled box broken in survival dropping one item, which, picked up and placed again, opens with the same contents; Circuit and both official servers give identical output
A creative player breaks a shulker box holding iron (one box item drops) and an empty one (nothing drops); Circuit and both official servers give identical output

12 steps of a survival player at a chiseled bookshelf facing south with a comparator behind it: a book clicked into each sixth of the front (upper and lower row, from the left: slots 0 to 5, each book used up), a book on a full slot taking its book back, an empty hand taking two books, a stick on an empty slot doing nothing and on a full one taking its book into the inventory; the slots, the held stack, the inventory and the comparator's last slot touched; Circuit and both official servers give identical output

A blast furnace cooks five raw gold; shift-clicking the ingots out gives 5 experience at the player (three orbs, level 0 with the official progress), putting them back none; a grindstone takes Efficiency III off an iron pickaxe and gives 11 to 21 experience (its amount draws from the level random) to the player standing on it; Circuit and both official servers give identical windows, pickups and experience

Experience orbs summoned around a player who stands still: those within 8 blocks come and are taken, one 12 blocks away stays, five at the feet are taken one by one, an orb of three is taken three times, and a large one gives 38 levels; Circuit and both official servers give the same pickups and set_experience values (progress bars equal as floats)

36 steps at a brewing stand: blaze powder shifted into the fuel slot and burned, stone and other ingredients into the ingredient slot, bottles one per slot and kept where they are when the bottle slots are full, stacks that do not swap, brews stopped and started by taking and putting ingredients, brewed bottles (also splash potions made with gunpowder) losing their custom color and rarity, results out to the hotbar's end and by key, the brew time and fuel properties; Circuit and both official servers give identical windows

A survival player fills empty maps at two places, turns, walks off and far from them, then copies, zooms to scale 4 and locks filled maps in a cartography table, with refused items, shift-clicks and a creative and a last empty map used: the window, the inventory with the map ids and each map's last data packet (scale, lock, markers, unexplored colors); Circuit and both official servers give identical output

A survival player holds filled maps over built terrain (pillars of eight blocks at five heights, a pool 1 to 12 deep, glass, waterlogged slabs, leaves, rails and grates, beds, wheat, blocks north of the map): a new map at the origin, the terrain changing under it, a map made far off and held 100 blocks away (the edge of the explored area), maps zoomed once and twice, a locked map and a map in the off hand; each map's colors after each step; Circuit and both official servers give identical output

The base color a held map drew on each official server for every block's default state, each state differing from it in one property, every waterlogged state likewise and blocks on their supports (6639 and 6538 states); evidence_tests checks Circuit's color of each

A new player joins, gets oak logs, crafts oak planks after /recipe took the recipe, fills ten slots, stands in water, cuts a cobblestone slab whose recipe was taken, sees a recipe, changes the books' settings, is given recipes (map extending, a known one, every one) and has one taken and given, joins again and has every recipe taken: per step the recipe-book packets (ids sorted within each and the packets sorted), each recipe's full entry, and the replies; Circuit and both official servers give identical output

79 steps placing recipes from the book in the own window, at crafting tables and in a furnace, blast furnace and smoker: once, once more and as many as fit (the stack each item fills, eggs and milk buckets), uneven stacks of the recipe, shapes centered and recipes too big for the grid, too few items (ghosts), full inventories, recipes of other kinds, a recipe not known, another window's id, the selected slot and creative mode; Circuit and both official servers give identical windows and ghosts

32 steps at a loom: pattern buttons in the tag's order (one beyond the list), layers in the dye's color, taking and shift-clicking results until the banners run out, a pattern item's single pattern chosen at once and dropped with it, a dye refused while another fills its slot, quick moves, a seventh layer; Circuit and both official servers give identical windows and banner pattern ids

cases.location: external: circuit-clienttest/packet-probe.js with weather-compare.txt, weather-join2.txt and (official only) weather-probe.txt, weather-timers.txt and weather-clear1.txt; Circuit's side also in tests/server/server_tests.cpp
